text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: Not reliably estimable from these facts

An all-women panel is not, by itself, evidence of sex bias. Both you and the successful candidate are women; nothing you’ve described establishes that sex influenced the decision. Assigning a percentage would invent precision.

Your qualifications warrant asking how the advertised criteria were applied, but paper counts and PhD status alone don’t determine merit; industry experience may legitimately matter.

Follow up on your written request. Ask for the assessment criteria, their weighting, feedback on your application, and any review deadlines. Check whether a completed PhD was mandatory and whether panel-composition rules apply. Raise specific procedural departures or evidence of unequal treatment—not assumptions based on the panel’s sex.
